objective.title: Read the Mission Brief
objective.description: Open the mission brief. It lists the kit, the exercise numbers, the net card and the operations checklist.

objective.title: Plan the Portable Station
objective.description: Choose a safe site, cable route, public clearance and weather plan. Then work out the energy plan from the kit: average power, energy used, energy left and whether the reserve holds.

params.question: Which of the following are typical duties of a Net Control Station?
options: Choose the regular net meeting time and frequency
Ensure that all stations checking into the net are properly licensed for operation on the net frequency
Call the net to order and direct communications between stations checking in
All these choices are correct
params.explanation: Net control organizes check-ins and directs communication between participating stations. It doesn't remove the other operators' responsibility for correct operation.

params.question: Which of the following is standard practice when you participate in a net?
options: When first responding to the net control station, transmit your call sign, name, and address as in the FCC database
Record the time of each of your transmissions
Unless you are reporting an emergency, transmit only when directed by the net control station
All these choices are correct
params.explanation: Ordinary net participation means transmitting when directed, with emergency reporting as the stated exception. Hearing a pause doesn't automatically make it your turn during a directed net.

objective.title: Diagnose the Station Fault
objective.description: Net control asks for full power. Set 50 W and key briefly: the radio resets and the log records both voltages. A meter on DC volts with its probes on the radio terminals holds the lowest voltage at the reset. Then key a short test at 5 W and read the battery terminals and the radio terminals while it transmits, and compare them.

params.question: What technique is used to ensure that voice messages containing unusual words are received correctly?
options: Send the words by voice and Morse code
Use the Q-code “QSR” to ask the receiving station to repeat the words back
Spell the words using a standard phonetic alphabet
All these choices are correct
params.explanation: Standard phonetics help convey unusual words accurately. Replacing a word with your own summary can change the message instead of clarifying it.

params.question: What is meant by “check” in a radiogram header?
options: The number of words or word equivalents in the text portion of the message
The call sign of the originating station
A list of stations that have relayed the message
A box on the message form that indicates that the message was received and/or relayed
params.explanation: The radiogram check counts words or word equivalents in the message text. It isn't a signal-strength report or a total including every part of the header.

params.question: The capstone starts with 120 Wh usable energy and needs a 30 Wh reserve. A 90-minute task averages 21.6 W. What energy remains before additional unlisted loads?
params.explanation: Ninety minutes is 1.5 hours, so consumption is 21.6 times 1.5, or 32.4 Wh. Subtracting that from 120 Wh leaves 87.6 Wh, which exceeds the stated reserve.

params.question: When do the FCC Part 97 Amateur Radio Service rules NOT apply to the operation of an amateur station?
options: When operating under RACES rules
When operating under FEMA rules
When operating under ARES rules
FCC rules always apply
params.explanation: FCC rules still apply during amateur operation, including emergencies. Specific provisions may address exceptional circumstances, but they don't switch the rules off.

params.question: Which of the following is a safety hazard of a 12-volt storage battery that lacks internal protection circuitry?
options: Touching both terminals with your hands can cause electrical shock
Shorting the terminals can cause burns, fire, or an explosion
RF emissions from a nearby transmitter can cause the electrolyte to emit poison gas
All these choices are correct
params.explanation: An unprotected 12 V battery can deliver enough short-circuit current to cause burns, fire or explosion. Low nominal voltage doesn't remove that stored-energy hazard.

params.question: A place name in a net message is unclear. What should you do before relaying it?
options: Replace it with a likely name.
Request a phonetic clarification.
Leave it out of the message.
Transmit over the next station.
params.explanation: Requesting a fill with standard phonetics preserves the intended place name. Guessing or omitting it changes the message rather than resolving the uncertainty.

params.question: Which of the following is an important safety precaution to observe when putting up an antenna tower?
options: Wear a ground strap connected to your wrist at all times
Insulate the base of the tower to avoid lightning strikes
Look for and stay clear of any overhead electrical wires
All these choices are correct
params.explanation: Overhead electrical wires must be identified and avoided before putting up an antenna structure. A location that is convenient for coverage can still be unsafe for installation.

params.question: Why is duty cycle one of the factors used to determine safe RF radiation exposure levels?
options: It affects the average exposure to radiation
It affects the peak exposure to radiation
It takes into account the antenna feed line loss
It takes into account the thermal effects of the final amplifier
params.explanation: Duty cycle affects average RF exposure during the relevant averaging period. A brief transmit interval and continuous transmission at the same power don't have the same average exposure.
